title: Crop Pest and Disease Control
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Walk the school or a nearby vegetable garden to find signs: holes in leaves, cut seedlings, curled leaves, wilting, spots, rot. Control by handpicking (gloves on), removing affected parts, uprooting and ash; no chemical sprays by learners.

skills.key_step: The child identifies vegetables attacked by pests (punctured leaves, cut seedlings, curled leaves: aphids, cutworms, caterpillars) and diseases (wilting, black and brown spots, rotting: blight, wilt, rots), tells a pest from a disease, and names controls.
steps: An animal seen: pest. Spots, rot, wilting: disease.

board.do: Draw a leaf with holes and one with brown spots.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a pest of vegetables?
misconceptions.repair: A pest is an animal you can see eating the crop; a disease shows as spots, rot or wilting caused by germs.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a disease of vegetables?
misconceptions.repair: Look at aphids through a hand lens: they are tiny insects, so they are pests.
Weeds hide pests and carry diseases; clear them and rotate crops.

misconceptions.ask: Kale seedlings are found cut off at soil level in the morning. What caused it?
misconceptions.repair: Dig gently round a cut seedling to find the curled grey cutworm.

checks.question: Give a sign of a crop disease.

skills.key_step: The child says how pests and diseases are controlled: handpick pests, remove and destroy affected parts away from the garden, uproot badly affected plants, use ash or natural sprays, rotate crops, keep tools clean, act early; chemicals only by trained adults.

floor.prerequisite: Can tell a pest from a disease.
floor.question: Is blight a pest or a disease?

representations: gloves and a tin for handpicking
steps: Find the pest or disease early.

board.do: Wait for "no, burn or bury them".

listen_for: Put them on the compost heap
misconceptions.ask: What is done with tomato plants killed by blight?
misconceptions.repair: Recall Grade 4: diseased plants spread disease through compost.

misconceptions.ask: How does crop rotation help control disease?
misconceptions.repair: Show a bed where tomatoes failed three years running.

misconceptions.ask: When is the best time to control pests?
misconceptions.repair: Show how a few aphids become thousands in two weeks.
Read the warning symbols on a pesticide label.

checks.question: How can aphids be controlled without chemicals?
checks.answer: handpicking, ash or a natural spray

checks.question: Why rotate crops?
checks.answer: so soil pests and diseases do not build up
